content: The case of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China (commonly known as the Alliance) on a charge of incitement to subversion has concluded 24 days of trial for Li Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, who deny the charges, with the verdict scheduled to be handed down on Friday, August 21. Chow Hang-tung, former vice-chair of the Alliance and a barrister, conducted her own defence in the case. Without access to a computer or the internet in prison, she wrote out her written submissions by hand over a hundred pages, one page at a time. At her application, the court played footage from two years of candlelight vigils for the June 4th Tiananmen Square crackdown, recreating bit by bit the candlelight in Victoria Park, along with testimony from witnesses of the June 4th events. "So I am the last defendant in this case, and also the last vice-chair of the first defendant, the Alliance... I am now 41 years old, a barrister, and there's nothing particularly remarkable about my background," Chow Hang-tung began, smiling as she spoke. Over the six days she gave evidence, she occasionally smiled, but also shed tears several times. What do the June 4th vigils and the call to "end one-party dictatorship" mean to Chow Hang-tung? What was her "intention"? This instalment of the podcast continues to take readers into the courtroom, recreating through voice Chow Hang-tung's testimony, as well as the judge's and the prosecution's cross-examination.
